chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who bequeathed her third, with which the debt of her brother's son is to be paid, and a portion for such-and-such male and such-and-such female, and I did not know how to handle that, so we went to Ibn Abi Layla. He said: So what did he say to you? I said: He said: They have nothing. So he said: He lied by Allah. They have one-tenth of the third.
ai.seo_question: How is the bequeathed third distributed when it covers both a specific debt and specific beneficiaries?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar* highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the Imam’s silence (which can imply correctness or mere lack of immediate elaboration) and the explicit ruling of the Umayyad judge Ibn Abi Layla, who determined that specific legatees receive one-tenth of the bequeathed third after debt settlement. It underscores the Shia scholarly appreciation for cross-school legal validation, where the narrator validates Ibn Abi Layla’s calculation as accurate ('correct') despite the Imam’s initial reserve, illustrating the practical application of the 'third' rule in estate distribution.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Ali bin Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abdullah bin Sinan, that he said:

I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, of a woman who bequeathed with her third, that the debt of the son of her brother is cleared with it, and that a part is for such-a-male and such-a-female, and I did not know (how to deal with) that, so we approached Ibn Abi Layla. He said: So what did he say to you? I said: He said: There is nothing to them. So he said: He has lied, by Allah. To them is a tenth of the third.
